scope: Conditional mathematical consequence of the exact frozen objective, using existing N/M/Q metadata. No graph/GT/query arrays opened, no new empirical experiment.
equations: For DeltaS=-k with integer k>=1, strict improvement iff DeltaC < k*M/(9Q)
For an individual node u, DeltaC <= D(u) = nonself_valid_out_slots(u)+nonself_valid_in_slots(u)
Thus any feasible candidate move with DeltaS<=-1 and D(u)<M/(9Q) is strictly improving regardless of the direction of its cut change.
Sum_u D(u)=2M, so #nodes with D(u)>=ceil(M/(9Q)) <= floor(2M/ceil(M/(9Q))).
confirmed: The globally normalized graph and fit-GT terms have unequal local scales; equal lambda=1 does not imply comparable per-node penalties.
limits: This sufficient condition concerns feasible candidate moves; it does not assert such a move exists or is selected.
Nodes absent from fit GT have DeltaS=0 and remain graph-only; a global degree bound does not bound the degree distribution of fit targets, which may be hubs.
No actual fit-target degree distribution or changed-node cut loss is measured by this derivation.
This is a mechanism hypothesis for observed fit-to-pilot nontransfer, not proof of its cause.
The P3 NOPASS gate remains fixed; this derivation does not authorize lambda tuning or another representation revision.
possible_falsifiable_followup: Only if the frozen target-support diagnosis warrants it, separately preregister a read-only graph-degree/fit-incidence audit to test whether the sufficient local-dominance condition covers actual fit targets and changing labels. Do not infer it from global average degree.
